clue.text: What a jury is expected to be as a precaution

definitions.text: What a jury is expected to be
definitions.meaning: a jury should be fair and impartial when it sits on a case, read as three words
the phrase means taking a step against a possible future need

explanation.surface: A remark on the duty of a jury, followed by a word about caution.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first part as JUST IN CASE: fair (just) while sitting in a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names preparing for an eventuality; split, the words describe fair jurors at a trial.

clue.text: Chine vessel found in cheap antique market

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed sailing ship of Chinese waters
worthless second-hand goods, as sold in a bric-a-brac shop

explanation.surface: A ship from China turns up among bric-a-brac at a cheap market.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'Chine', a cut of meat, where the clue means 'Chinese'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the Chinese sailing ship and slang for old rubbish of little value.

clue.text: Apparently very hard hearing of hearing

annotationWithheld.why: Printed as 'Apparently very hard hearing of hearing (5,4)': the words are garbled (likely 'Apparently very hard of hearing'), with no scan to confirm
annotationWithheld.clue: Apparently very hard hearing of hearing

clue.text: Excellent proposal by one who holds all the cards

definitions.meaning: perfect, the best that could be

definitions.text: proposal by one who holds all the cards
definitions.meaning: a card dealer might announce that it is their turn to hand out the pack, read as two words

explanation.surface: A fine suggestion from a player who has every card in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as I DEAL: what the person holding the whole pack says before handing it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal means perfect; as two words it is the dealer's statement at a card table.

clue.text: Make one's debut as a striker

definitions.meaning: a debutante formally enters society for the first time
workers who strike walk off the job together

explanation.surface: A first appearance made by a footballer who scores goals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' suggests a footballer, but it is a worker going on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutante is said to enter society this way, and a union calls its members off work with the same phrase.

clue.text: Type men as game dogs

definitions.meaning: printers who arrange type for printing (typesetters)
breeds of gun dog used to point out game birds

explanation.surface: A description of men who look like hunting dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type men' reads as 'kind of men', but it means men who set printing type.
explanation.definitionFit: Compositors set type, and the Irish and English breeds are gun dogs that crouch to mark birds.

clue.text: To give criminal aid is a bit of a gamble

parts.note: a small wager, a single flutter

explanation.surface: Helping a criminal is risky.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist or encourage someone in wrongdoing, as in the legal phrase 'aid and abet'.

clue.text: What the violinist did during and after his performance

definitions.text: What the violinist did during and after his performance

parts.words: What the violinist did during and after his performance
parts.note: a violinist draws a bow across the strings while playing, then bends forward to the applause afterwards

explanation.surface: A question about a violinist's conduct at a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both drawing the bow over strings and bending at the waist to an audience.

clue.text: Relevant instruction for plugging in electric lead

definitions.meaning: pertinent, bearing on the matter

definitions.text: instruction for plugging in electric lead
definitions.meaning: a lead goes into a power socket, which the British call a power point

explanation.surface: Advice on connecting an appliance to the mains.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a wall socket is a 'power point', so the lead goes 'to the point'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means pertinent; read literally it directs a plug towards the socket.

clue.text: It sheds seeds when it breaks and opens

definitions.text: It sheds seeds when it breaks and opens

indicators.note: breaking the words up lets their letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A seed case bursts and scatters its seeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' rearranges AND OPENS; the whole clue also describes the laxative plant's pod splitting.
explanation.definitionFit: The seed case of the cassia plant, which splits open to release seeds.

clue.text: Snare ducks in the North and South East

indicators.note: the ducks sit inside the compass letters

parts.note: SE is the abbreviation for south-east
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so two ducks are two O's

explanation.surface: Trapping waterfowl across northern and south-eastern England.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop of cord used to catch animals is a kind of trap.

clue.text: Parental humour is just common sense

parts.note: a mother is a parent, used here as a modifier

explanation.surface: A claim that a parent's jokes are no more than plain sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The old phrase names native good sense, the practical wisdom one is born with.

clue.text: Commendation which is anything but rare

definitions.meaning: words of praise, as for a good job
cooked through, the opposite of a bloody steak

explanation.surface: Praise for something that is not unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rare' seems to mean uncommon, but it is the steak barely cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a cry of praise and also describes meat cooked thoroughly.

clue.text: Elbow string worn by stripper in the nude

indicators.note: the letter sits inside the word for unclothed

parts.note: in the nude means unclothed, naked
a G-string is the skimpy garment of a striptease artist

explanation.surface: A stripper in the nude, wearing only a G-string, uses an elbow.
explanation.definitionFit: To elbow someone is to poke or jostle them with the arm.

clue.text: Lean body against easel when all paintings have been mounted?

definitions.meaning: a thin, wiry physique

definitions.text: against easel when all paintings have been mounted?
definitions.meaning: an unused picture surround left propped by the easel once every canvas is in place

explanation.surface: Propping a thin figure against an easel after the paintings are hung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lean' looks like a verb (prop), but it is the adjective thin; SPARE also means left over.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare means thin and also surplus; a frame is a body's build and a picture surround.

clue.text: Excuse the foreword

definitions.meaning: a false reason given to cover the real one
the matter before the main text of a book, as two parts

explanation.surface: A book's opening passage offered as an apology.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretext is a cover story; split as PRE-TEXT it is what precedes the text.

clue.text: Lift to reveal structure

indicators.note: structuring the letters builds them into a new shape

explanation.surface: Lifting a cover to expose a building's framework.
explanation.definitionFit: A lift is the British word for the American cage that carries people between floors.

clue.text: Treble appeal launched by new parson

indicators.note: a new version of the word has its letters remade

parts.note: O is an exclamation of appeal, as in 'O Lord'

explanation.surface: A fresh vicar launches a fundraising appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appeal' suggests a fundraising drive, but it is the pleading cry O; 'launched by' simply puts it after the remade clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy treble sings the highest part, the same range as a female soprano voice.

clue.text: Water a farrowed sow

parts.note: a sow that has farrowed (given birth to piglets) is a mother, a dam
a sow is a female pig, a swine

explanation.surface: A pig that has given birth is watered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water' looks like a verb but is the noun. A DAM'S WINE is the drink of the first man, plain water.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain drinking water is called Adam's wine (or Adam's ale), the drink of the first man.

clue.text: Beams for the Kon-Tiki voyagers?

definitions.meaning: sloping timbers that hold up a roof
Thor Heyerdahl's crew crossed the Pacific on a balsa raft in 1947

explanation.surface: Roof timbers for a famous ocean expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kon-Tiki was a raft, so its crew were RAFT-ERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Roof timbers share their name with people who travel by raft.

clue.text: Old musical instrument distinguished by its scales

definitions.meaning: a curved wooden wind instrument of the Renaissance
a snake is covered in scales

explanation.surface: An antique instrument famed for the scales played on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scales' suggests music, but they are a snake's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The snake-shaped bass horn and the reptile itself share a name.

clue.text: Provide new guttering for sand-laden storm

definitions.meaning: to fit the house with drains again
rain stained by Saharan dust blown north

explanation.surface: Replacing gutters ahead of a dusty downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-drain is to supply drainage again; red rain is a shower coloured by desert dust.

clue.text: Ask rich sort for oriental transport

indicators.note: to sort the words is to put their letters in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Ask a wealthy person for a ride in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: A light hooded cart pulled by a runner, used in Japan and elsewhere in Asia.

clue.text: Flower-girl?

parts.note: a woman's name that is also the Roman goddess of blossom and the word for plant life

explanation.surface: A girl who sells blossoms.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman goddess of blooms and a girl's name, the term for an area's plant life.

clue.text: Drunk but unlikely to cause friction

definitions.meaning: tipsy, well lubricated
greased, so parts slide smoothly

explanation.surface: A drunk who is too easy-going to start a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'friction' suggests a row between people; it is the rubbing of machine parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for intoxicated, and literally lubricated so parts run smoothly.

clue.text: Resort to which trainee sappers are sent

definitions.meaning: a source of help one turns to

definitions.text: to which trainee sappers are sent
definitions.meaning: sappers are the Royal Engineers (RE), and trainees go on a course

explanation.surface: A holiday spot where army engineers are sent to train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' suggests a holiday spot but means a fallback. Sappers are the Royal Engineers, RE, who go on a COURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Recourse is a fallback one turns to; split, it is an RE course.

clue.text: Employing one in manufacture of guns

indicators.note: the single numeral goes inside the remade weapon word
manufacturing the word builds its letters into something new

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Hiring someone to make guns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manufacture of' rearranges GUNS into USNG, and 'in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be making use of something is to be employing it.

clue.text: Measure of resistance applied to official letters

definitions.meaning: units of electrical resistance
On Her Majesty's Service, printed on British government mail

explanation.surface: Gauging opposition to official correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: British government post was marked OHMS, On Her Majesty's Service.
explanation.definitionFit: Units of electrical resistance; also the initials stamped on British state mail.

clue.text: The entire audience taken on in open challenge

definitions.meaning: everyone who comes along
a contest open to any challenger at all

explanation.surface: A whole crowd accepts an open challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means everyone who turns up, as when a boxer at a fair offers to fight anyone.

clue.text: Part of the fair is Hibernian

definitions.text: Part of the fair is Hibernian

indicators.note: only a portion of the run of words is taken, letters lying across them

explanation.surface: Some of the fair-haired are from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'faIR IS Hibernian'; Hibernia is Latin for Ireland, and fair hair is common there.
explanation.definitionFit: Hibernian is a formal word for things from Ireland, from its Latin name.

clue.text: Creator of Christian Science's current revolution

definitions.meaning: Mary Baker ... founded the Christian Science church in 1879
water circling against the main stream

explanation.surface: The founder of a church brings about a modern revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like 'modern', but it is a flow of water, and 'revolution' is a turning.
explanation.definitionFit: The religious founder's surname is also a whirlpool in a stream.

clue.text: Unknown people about fifty become homicidal maniacs

indicators.note: the unknown people surround the Roman numeral

parts.note: strangers are people one does not know
L is the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: Unfamiliar men of about fifty become murderers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about fifty' looks like an age; 'about' puts L inside STRANGERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Killers who choke their victims are a kind of murderous maniac.
